No, class action lawsuits are very helpful and often the only tool the consumers have to fight against a large corporation. Sure, you could get more money if you sue individually, but most individuals don't have the resources necessary to do that, because they can just drown you in formalities. But that's not the point. A large corporation will happily pay you a few grands to shut up already, that's nothing to them. But class action lawsuits are often worth millions or billions and can seriously affect the company's business.

Just look at the recent VW scandal. They are handing out $1000 vouchers to VW owners in North America because they know there will be very expensive class action lawsuits. And in Europe, where the same cars have been sold? The affected owners get nothing, since there are no class action lawsuits. VW knows that every owner has to sue individually and has to prove his car doesn't meet the standard it was advertised with. Almost nobody will be able to do that, so VW is like, if you want something, just try to sue us, we don't care about you.

That's why class action lawsuits are great and I wish they were possible in Europe. You may not become rich, but it's a good tool to remind companies about their liabilities. And you also can get some compensation with minimal risk, without having to fight hordes of lawyers on your own.
